stories.headline: Starmer tensions with Trump escalate over Iran conflict as UK-US relations strain
stories.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer publicly criticized Trump and Putin for driving up UK energy costs, saying he's 'fed up' with their impact. Trump responded by comparing Starmer to Neville Chamberlain and criticizing UK's refusal to support US military action in Iran. The UK declined to join Trump's naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, leading to a significant deterioration in UK-US relations.

stories.headline: UK shelves Chagos Islands handover to Mauritius after Trump withdraws support
stories.summary: The UK government put its plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius on hold after Donald Trump's administration withdrew support for the deal. The legislation has been removed from the upcoming King's Speech, effectively killing the agreement that would have resolved the long-running territorial dispute.

stories.headline: UK Defense Secretary Healey reveals month-long operation tracking Russian spy submarines
stories.summary: Defense Secretary John Healey disclosed that UK forces tracked three Russian submarines conducting surveillance of undersea cables and pipelines in the North Atlantic for a month before they retreated. Healey directly warned Putin 'we see you' and said any attempt to damage UK infrastructure would have serious consequences.

stories.headline: King Charles US state visit proceeds despite UK-US tensions over Iran
stories.summary: King Charles and Queen Camilla will visit the US April 27-30 for America's 250th anniversary celebrations, despite strained UK-US relations over the Iran conflict. The visit is seen as an attempt to salvage diplomatic ties, with Charles expected to play a key role in maintaining the special relationship.

stories.headline: Kemi Badenoch proposes largest peacetime rearmament program to strengthen UK defense
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called for 'the biggest peacetime programme of rearmament in our country's history,' including increasing the British army by 20,000 troops. She proposed reinstating the two-child benefit cap to fund the defense spending increases, criticizing the government's preparedness for Middle East conflicts.

stories.headline: Chancellor Reeves warns Iran war will impose economic costs on UK households and businesses
stories.summary: Chancellor Rachel Reeves announced she will outline plans to help businesses struggling with high energy prices caused by the Iran conflict. She warned that the war will 'come at a cost' for British families and businesses, with gas prices rising sharply during the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Nigel Farage's Reform UK faces scrutiny over energy bill competition and deputy leader's tax affairs
stories.summary: Police are reviewing complaints about Reform UK's energy bills competition after Nigel Farage was accused of awarding the prize to supporters he already knew. Separately, deputy leader Richard Tice faces allegations that his company failed to pay £91,000 in tax on dividends, with calls for Farage to dismiss him.

stories.headline: Justice Secretary Lammy extends time limit for challenging lenient sentences from 28 days to six months
stories.summary: David Lammy announced changes to allow victims and bereaved families six months instead of 28 days to challenge 'unduly lenient' sentences. The change recognizes that traumatized families cannot be expected to engage with the justice system immediately after a conviction. The move has been welcomed by campaigners.

stories.headline: Bank of England warns supermarkets may introduce 'surge pricing' as retailers adopt dynamic pricing technology
stories.summary: The Bank of England warned that supermarkets could introduce dynamic pricing that allows them to increase costs when demand is high, similar to Uber's surge pricing. Around a third of UK businesses plan to adopt algorithm-driven pricing tools by early 2027, up from one in five currently.

stories.headline: GCHQ warns Russian hackers are hijacking UK wifi routers for espionage operations
stories.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre warned that Russian state-linked hackers from the Fancy Bear group are compromising wifi routers in British homes and offices to harvest passwords and credentials. The operation targets commonly used routers from manufacturers like TP-Link and MikroTik.

stories.headline: Actor John Nolan, Christopher Nolan's uncle and Batman star, dies at 87
stories.summary: British actor John Nolan, who appeared in Batman films and TV series Person of Interest, died at age 87. He was the uncle of directors Christopher and Jonathan Nolan, appearing in several of their projects including Batman Begins, The Dark Knight Rises, and Dunkirk. His most notable role was as former MI6 agent John Greer in Person of Interest.

stories.headline: Keanu Reeves stars in new Apple TV comedy 'Outcome' alongside Cameron Diaz and Matt Bomer
stories.summary: Keanu Reeves premieres in the dark comedy film 'Outcome,' directed by Jonah Hill, where he plays a Hollywood star whose career is threatened by blackmail. The film marks his first collaboration with Cameron Diaz in 30 years and features appearances by Martin Scorsese. Reviews have been mixed, giving Reeves one of his worst Rotten Tomatoes scores since 2018.
